clue.text: Head first

definitions.meaning: the person in charge of a school or college
foremost, chief in importance

explanation.surface: A two-word instruction to go in head first, as a diver might.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's head teacher is its principal, and the principal reason is the chief or foremost one.

clue.text: Girl has bearing of aristocrat

parts.note: Patricia is a girl's name
N, north, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A young woman carries herself like a noble.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome a member of the hereditary noble class was so called, and the word now means any noble.

clue.text: Patriarch of York, one was

definitions.meaning: one of the founding fathers of Israel in Genesis
... of York is the Jewish moneylender in Scott's novel Ivanhoe

explanation.surface: A venerable elder who came from York.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham's son is one of the biblical patriarchs, and Scott's moneylender in Ivanhoe carries the same name.

clue.text: Main attraction, for nosy characters put right outside

indicators.note: the remedy word sits outside, enclosing the other letters

parts.note: to cure is to put right

indicators.note: the letters of the word nosy taken as characters in a new order

explanation.surface: The chief draw for busybodies is set right outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' signals the letters of 'nosy' rearranged, and 'outside' wraps the remedy word round them. The comma after 'attraction' is a link; the definition is the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre of attention or admiration, originally the Pole Star that guided sailors' eyes.

clue.text: Reverence for person based on this?

definitions.text: Reverence for person based on this?

parts.words: Reverence for person based on this?
parts.note: worship of someone is described as setting them up on a base, like a statue

explanation.surface: Asking what foundation lies under admiration for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'to put someone on a pedestal' means to idolise them; the base a statue stands on is what the clue asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: The base on which a statue stands is the plinth in the idiom about idolising someone.

clue.text: German ruler beheaded University man

indicators.note: removing the head means taking the first letter away from the ruler's title

parts.note: an Elector was a prince entitled to choose the Holy Roman Emperor

explanation.surface: A German prince is decapitated by an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' drops the first letter of ELECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecturer or reader at some universities, especially abroad, holds this title.

clue.text: One of those setting standard was an architect

definitions.meaning: a member of the family neighbours try to keep up with, in the idiom about matching others' lifestyle
Inigo ..., the seventeenth-century English architect

explanation.surface: Someone who once set the standard in building design was an architect.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense comes from the idiom 'keeping up with the Joneses', the neighbours whose lifestyle sets the standard; the second is Inigo Jones, who designed the Banqueting House in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The family others try to keep up with in the idiom bears this surname, which also belonged to the architect Inigo.

clue.text: A humorous writer, first and last

definitions.meaning: the author of Three Men in a Boat
his forename and surname are the same word

explanation.surface: A comic author, from beginning to end.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerome K. Jerome, author of the comic novel Three Men in a Boat, had the same first name and surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian comic novelist of Three Men in a Boat used this name as both forename and surname.

clue.text: Enter it if this queen ordered

indicators.note: the letters are put in a different order to give the name

explanation.surface: An instruction to admit a queen if she is commanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges ENTER IT IF.
explanation.definitionFit: Akhenaten's wife was the Egyptian queen famed for her painted bust.

clue.text: Draws up musical direction for David

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: hales means hauls or draws

explanation.surface: Someone sketches a musical instruction for a boy named David.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns HALES round. King David is traditionally the author of the Psalms, where this word appears as a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew word recurring in the Psalms is thought to be an instruction to the musicians.

clue.text: Aimed to be prepared for race

definitions.meaning: a gun pointed at a target has been levelled at it
an athlete or horse got fit for a contest

explanation.surface: Someone set their sights on getting ready for a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon levelled at a target is pointed at it, and an athlete coached for a contest has been made fit.

clue.text: Attentive, but no longer anxious

definitions.meaning: taking pains, paying close attention
an obsolete sense: full of worry, which the word once meant

explanation.surface: Someone who pays attention but has stopped worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' marks an archaic sense: the word once meant full of care in the sense of worried, so the clue looks contradictory but is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes pains is attentive; in older English the same word meant full of worry, a sense now obsolete.

clue.text: Race scattered about in South America

indicators.note: letters scattered about are strewn into a new order, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about
taken as written

explanation.surface: A people dispersed around South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges C (circa, 'about'), IN and SA; the surface fits the answer, a South American people, neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andean people of the pre-Columbian empire form an ethnic group, which older usage calls a race.

clue.text: Music for army, not for fleet

definitions.text: Music for army, not for fleet

parts.words: Music for army, not for fleet
parts.note: music for soldiers on parade at a stately pace; fleet here means swift, not a navy

explanation.surface: Military music meant for soldiers rather than sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleet' seems to set the navy against the army, but it means fast: this parade tune is for unhurried troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial military pace and its accompanying tune are deliberately unhurried, the opposite of fleet or swift.

clue.text: Pass on knowledge with which a learner's familiar

parts.note: to pass on knowledge is to tell or apprise
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Teaching something a student already knows.
explanation.definitionFit: Familiar here means casual and relaxed, as in an easy, unceremonious manner.

clue.text: Anticipate Nottingham team completely

parts.note: Nottingham Forest is the city's football club
all means wholly, completely

explanation.surface: Predicting a Nottingham side's full results.
explanation.walkthrough: Nottingham Forest is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in advance so as to prevent something is to pre-empt it.

clue.text: Tendency to be found in wood

definitions.meaning: a leaning or inclination
the weighting in a bowl, the ball used in lawn bowls, called a wood

explanation.surface: An inclination that grows in the grain of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: In lawn bowls (a British green game) the balls are called woods, and each is weighted so it curves; that weighting has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaning or prejudice is a tendency, and a bowls ball's built-in curve is its weighting.

clue.text: Indicate a party subscriber

parts.note: to sign is to indicate by gesture
the Tory party is the UK Conservative party

explanation.surface: Pointing out a member who pays for a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: One who subscribes, in the old sense of writing a name beneath a document, puts a signature to it.

clue.text: Fifty opponents at first covered city

indicators.note: at is placed first, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
antis are people against something

explanation.surface: Fifty rivals initially concealed a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered' means submerged: the legendary island city sank beneath the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato's legendary island city was swallowed up by the ocean, so waters cover it.

clue.text: Something detested about 1000 articles

indicators.note: the articles go round the number, enclosing it

parts.note: an, a and the are the grammatical articles, with a used twice
an, a and the are the grammatical articles, with a used twice
an, a and the are the grammatical articles, with a used twice
an, a and the are the grammatical articles, with a used twice
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A thousand items that someone loathes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the four articles round the Roman thousand; 'articles' supplies all four pieces, with the indefinite article used in both its forms.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing or person cursed or loathed, originally one formally excommunicated by the church.

clue.text: Andy's predecessor in French part?

parts.note: a French region whose name ends in the boy's name Andy; the clue asks for the letters coming before it

explanation.surface: Asking who came before Andy in some French role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'predecessor' suggests someone who held a post before Andy, but it means the letters before ANDY in the name of the northern French region; those letters also make a word for a standard.
explanation.definitionFit: The letters in front of Andy in the region by the Channel spell a word meaning a usual standard.

clue.text: Lasting reputation

definitions.meaning: permanent, enduring
status or repute in a community

explanation.surface: A good name that endures.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent committee is a standing one, and one's status in society is one's standing.

clue.text: Capital part for female academic

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A London district suited to a woman scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: Hendon is a district of north London, home of the Metropolitan Police training college.
explanation.definitionFit: The suburb in north-west London is a district of the British capital.

clue.text: Who had special seat on a Jumbo?

indicators.note: special treatment of the letters gives them a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Asking who got a privileged seat on a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges WHO HAD. Jumbo looks like the aircraft but is the elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: The canopied seat strapped on an elephant's back carries riders in India.

clue.text: Heroine murdered in play made end so awful

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A stage heroine is killed because the play's ending was so dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges MADE END SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello's wife is the heroine smothered by her jealous husband in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Turn up second old Impressionist painter

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the letters from the bottom

parts.note: aged means old

explanation.surface: A veteran Impressionist arrives in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' reverses S + AGED (SAGED) in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar of that surname was the French artist famous for ballet dancers, exhibiting with the Impressionists.

clue.text: Back in Bengal batting, beaten by Indians

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Indian cricketers batting in Bengal are defeated in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks letters hidden across 'Bengal batting', and 'Back' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: The small paired hand drum of North Indian music is played with the fingers and palms.

clue.text: Not a major route like Oxford Street

definitions.meaning: a ... is a secondary road in Britain
wide, as a great shopping street is

explanation.surface: A London thoroughfare that is not a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are graded A (major) and B (minor); a B road read as one word gives the answer. Oxford Street, London's shopping street, is wide.
explanation.definitionFit: A British minor road is classed B, and a wide street like Oxford Street is ample in width.

clue.text: Cautious as Alice's intended, Edward

parts.note: in A. A. Milne's poem about Buckingham Palace, Alice is marrying one of the guard
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Alice's fiancé Edward is a careful sort.
explanation.walkthrough: In A. A. Milne's poem 'Buckingham Palace', Christopher Robin and Alice watch the guard change, and 'Alice is marrying one of the guard'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wary and reserved in what they say is circumspect, keeping their thoughts protected.

clue.text: Artist's connexion with sport

parts.note: a tie is a link or bond
polo is the sport played on horseback

explanation.surface: A painter's link to the sporting world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist's' reads as possessive but stands for 'Artist is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista of that surname was the Venetian rococo painter of grand frescoes.

clue.text: Wise man's point on one's performance

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a performance by one person alone is a solo
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A sage makes a point about a one-man show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise man's' stands for 'Wise man is'; the Athenian lawgiver's name became a word for a wise legislator.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian lawgiver's name is used generally for any sage statesman.

clue.text: Farmer's activity as a union man?

definitions.meaning: the cultivation of land and rearing of animals
whimsically, what a married man does, union meaning marriage

explanation.surface: Asking whether farming counts as trade-union work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union man' suggests a trade unionist, but the union is marriage: the second sense is the role of a married man.
explanation.definitionFit: Agricultural cultivation and stockbreeding has this name, which jokingly suggests the conduct of a spouse.
